key_insight: A deterministic multi-agent framework can reduce two safety risks in AI medical reasoning: rushing to diagnosis too early and sending out uncertain or divergent answers.
clinical_relevance: By enforcing complete symptom collection and screening for high-uncertainty outputs, the approach aims to make LLM-based healthcare assistants more reliable before patient-facing use.
method: Uses a neuro-symbolic gate to require full OLDCARTS symptom capture before diagnostic handoff.
Applies an epistemic uncertainty gate based on semantic entropy across 5 independent diagnostic samples.
Replaces LLM-as-a-judge routing with deterministic orchestration constraints.
evidence_signal: In 150 simulated test cases, the full system reached 49.3% diagnostic precision, an 11.3-point absolute gain over baseline, with OLDCARTS completeness negatively correlated with semantic entropy (r = -0.181, p < 0.05).
watch_item: Results come from simulated patients and one model setup, so real-world clinical performance, generalizability, and workflow integration still need validation.
paper_title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
